decision.title: XSLT on the newest draft: nothing moved; typed="~T" (packet 4.22)

body.p: , after , , , , . Verified as asks: the debug preset, the touched unit and CLI tests (xslt, the cli/transform tests), clang-tidy and the call-cycle check, the grammars/xslt_pattern corpus (101 of 101), and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver before and after, case by case.

item.p: Drafts (fetched 2026-10-20; not vendored, as no spec copy is kept, ): the XSLT 4.0, XPath 4.0, XQuery 4.0 and F&O 4.0 editor's drafts at qt4cg.org/specifications/ (xslt-40/Overview.html, xquery-40/xpath-40.html, xquery-40/xquery-40.html, xpath-functions-40/Overview.html) are all dated 13 October 2026, built from qt4cg/qtspecs master 72f2229 (2026-10-13; the last merges are PRs 2977, 2966, 2931, 2920 and 2911). That is the draft already targets: the grammars and the lowering need no change.

Suite: qt4cg/xslt40-test master is 91328fb (2026-10-13), the commit already vendored (). A checkout of it equals third_party/xslt40-test apart from the parts the update script leaves out, so tools/update-test-suites.sh has nothing to move and was not run; third_party/xslt40-test.commit is unchanged.

XT40: 11,945 passed + 130 wrong error at 55d40c5 (before); 11,951 + 130 at aae4d04 (after), 437 failed, 0 errors. The six changed cases (result-document-0201, -0212, -0285, -0286, -0287, transform-009) are 7.20's 638871f, class (a). The XT40 section of docs/CONFORMANCE.md and README's row are from the aae4d04 run.
Class (b), the newest draft wins (57 cases, recorded here):

"~T" type patterns, 53 (48 failed, 5 wrong error): XSLT 4.0 6.3.1 and Appendix E have no TypePattern (PR 2911 replaced it with atomic(), record(), map, array and JNode patterns); XTSE0340 stays. priority-010, -012 to -018, -020, -030 to -033, -100 to -109, -120 to -122, -142, -160 to -162; array-023, -024; arrays-010, -024; match-409, -410, -411; mode-4008; next-match-401 to -406, -420; record-022; transform-401; type-alias-008, -009, -010, -013, -014, -015. The draft's own examples still write "~T" (6.4.7, 6.6 and 6.9.6); the grammar decides.

Default priorities, 4: priority-002 (".[2=2]" is +0.5 by 6.4.2, the suite says 1.0), -124 and -141 ("{'x'}" and "{42}" are 0 by 6.4.4, "array(P)" is P's by 6.4.6; the suite says 0.25), -163 ("jnode(42, {*})" is +0.5 by 6.4.7, constant selector; the suite says 0). Every other form agrees: a scratch check of the suite's expectations rewritten in the draft's syntax (atomic(xs:int) 0.4375, array(atomic(xs:integer)) 0.25, jnode(42, atomic(xs:integer)) 0.5, {} 0.5, and so on) passed in all 24 forms tried.

The draft allows what the suite still refuses (XTSE0340), 2: match-080 ("/key('k', 42)//a": "/" RelativePathExprP with a FunctionCallP, 6.3.2) and match-239 ("(.[...])": ParenthesizedPattern holds any Pattern, 6.3.2).

Class (c): none found among the cases examined (the priority set, the XTSE0340 cluster). The other failures were not examined one by one: they are the open causes of , , and (class (a), not done), for example fn:apply-templates (6.9.3.1, 5 cases) and enclosing modes (6.9.6, 8 cases).

Done (class a, from the draft without a suite case): 6.9.4's typed="~T" on xsl:mode (sxml raised XTSE0020). The reader's value syntax KEYWORD_OR_ITEM_TYPE reads "~" and an ItemType as an item type, anything else as a keyword; such a mode gets typed 3, element names stay names, and a typed rule of its own ('s mechanism) whose match function is not(. instance of T) raises XTTE3100. "unspecified" stays ~item(). Two declarations of one precedence with different types are not compared (XTSE0545), as as types are not. Two corpus tests pin "~T" in patterns as an error.
Left: nothing for 4.22. When qtspecs or xslt40-test next move, refresh both together () and run this classification again.
